source: vendored Triangle engine (pipeline/sim/vendor/teto), res.rawGarbage per lock — attack before cancellation
denominators: pieces = results.stats.piecesplaced (the replay's, never the engine lock count); opener pieces = min(pieces, window_pieces) per round, mid = the rest; players[].attack is the replay's garbage.attack, windows[].attack is the engine's and differs from it only in anchor.attack.exceptions
components_mean: base = TETR.IO table value; b2b = integer back-to-back level; combo = the combo multiplier's addition; allclear = the Perfect Clear's own garbage entry; residual = engine attack beyond that integer model (garbage multiplier past garbagemargin, fractional b2b level). The five sum to the engine attack exactly.
not_eligible_because: attack per clear and its component split come from one engine with no second implementation
garbage_tspins_mean: a full T-spin (TSS, TSD or TST; minis excluded) whose clear removed at least one garbage row. A garbage row is full but for its one hole, so a lock that clears it filled that hole: the T went into the garbage hole. rows = the garbage rows those T-spins cleared. Which lock cleared a garbage row is the engine's; the per-round total of garbage rows cleared is anchored against the replay's garbage.cleared (anchor.garbage_cleared)
